response.text:
Short answer: the sender does not see anything different. Archiving vs deleting only changes what happens in your mailbox/account — it doesn’t notify the sender or change the copy they have.

More detail (general terms and common providers like Gmail/Outlook/IMAP):

- Visibility to the sender
  - Neither archiving nor deleting a message from your mailbox sends a notification to the sender. Their copy (for example, the message in their Sent folder) is unchanged.

- What archiving does
  - Moves the message out of your Inbox/focused view but keeps it in your account.
  - It’s still stored and searchable (often in "All Mail" or an "Archive" folder).
  - It’s recoverable and not permanently removed; replies to that thread will usually return the conversation to your Inbox.
  - Good when you want to remove clutter but keep the record.

- What deleting does
  - Removes the message from your Inbox and places it in Trash/Deleted Items.
  - Trash may be auto-emptied after a retention period (e.g., Gmail: 30 days) or when you manually empty it; some systems keep Deleted Items until you purge them.
  - Once permanently deleted (and after backups/retention windows expire) it’s typically unrecoverable for you.
  - Deleting only affects your copy — other recipients and the sender still retain their copies.

- Provider/protocol nuances
  - Gmail: "Archive" removes the Inbox label (message stays in All Mail). "Delete" moves to Trash, then permanent deletion after 30 days.
  - Outlook/Exchange: archiving usually moves to an Archive folder; deletion moves to Deleted Items (retention depends on server policy).
  - IMAP: archive commonly moves the message to an Archive folder; delete marks it for deletion and it’s removed on expunge. POP typically downloads a local copy so server-side archive/delete behavior may differ.
  - Shared mailboxes or delegated accounts: deleting a message from a shared mailbox can remove it for all users who access that same mailbox.

- Other things to be aware of
  - Backups / retention policies: even “permanently” deleted mail may persist for a time in provider backups or under org data-retention policies.
  - Read receipts, delivery status, or sender-side logs are not affected by your archiving/deleting.
  - If you’ve downloaded the message (or others forwarded it), copies may exist elsewhere.

If you tell me which email provider (Gmail, Outlook/Exchange, Apple Mail, etc.) you use, I can give the exact behavior and steps for archiving vs deleting there.
